TemplateStylesExtenderCustomPropertiesDe.description: Allow CSS custom properties (CSS variables) to be declared as properties

TemplateStylesExtenderExtendCustomProper.description: Allow the CSS custom properties (CSS variables) to be used as values in all properties. Not every var() depends on this. css-sanitizer accepts var() as a whole colour and inside a colour function, so color: var(--c, red) and color: rgb(var(--r) 0 0) keep working whatever this is set to. Turning it off removes var() from everywhere else, including width: var(--w), transform: translateX(var(--x)), and the colour a relative colour starts from, color: rgb(from var(--c) r g b).

TemplateStylesExtenderEnableUnscopingSup.description: Allow to unscope css by changing '.mw-parser-output' to a custom class

TemplateStylesExtenderRequireFontFamilyP.description: Require @font-face family names to start with 'TemplateStyles', as TemplateStyles itself does. Off by default, which is this extension's long-standing behaviour. Note that @font-face is not scoped to .mw-parser-output, so a family declared in a TemplateStyles page applies to the whole rendered page, including skin chrome; enabling this restores TemplateStyles' namespacing. Changing this does not invalidate already-rendered pages, which keep their previous CSS until purged.

TemplateStylesExtenderUnscopingPermissio.description: Specify the permission a user must have to use unscoping. Defaults to 'editinterface'.

TemplateStylesExtenderAllowExternalResou.description: Allow url(), image-set() and the other external-resource functions inside custom property (--*) values. False by default, which keeps the security-advisory behaviour of rejecting them (a var()-composed URL cannot be checked against $wgTemplateStylesAllowedUrls at parse time). Enable only on a wiki whose enforced Content-Security-Policy restricts these fetches to trusted hosts: a custom property is substituted into the fetching property at render time (e.g. mask-image: var(--x)), so with the flag on that fetch is never checked against the allowlist and CSP is the sole guard for it. That is the point of the flag, so do not enable it without such a CSP. A URL written directly in a typed property (background-image: url(...)) stays allowlist-checked whatever the flag holds, but that is not the path the flag opens.
